l4_steps.name: Receive Shipper DG Declaration & Air Waybill
l4_steps.input: Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods (IATA DGR Sec 8.1.6 format), Air Waybill
l4_steps.output: DG shipment record created in cargo system with initial classification flag
l4_steps.kpi: DG acceptance processing time ≤30 min per shipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete or incorrectly completed shipper declarations are the leading cause of DG non-compliance; IATA DGR Sec 8.1.6 mandates specific formats but non-industry shippers routinely submit non-conforming documents requiring full re-inspection

l4_steps.name: Validate UN Number and Proper Shipping Name
l4_steps.system: IATA DGR e-Tool (electronic dangerous goods database)
l4_steps.input: UN number and proper shipping name from shipper's declaration
l4_steps.output: DG classification confirmed or rejected; discrepancy report if mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: Classification error rate <0.5% of DG shipments processed
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR is revised annually; local DGR lookup databases at handling agents may lag the official publication by 4–8 weeks, causing classification mismatches particularly for newly added UN numbers in Class 9

l4_steps.name: Verify Packing Group, Quantity Limits & Label Compliance
l4_steps.input: Physical package inspection, shipper's declaration packing details
l4_steps.output: Packing compliance report; label and marking verification sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: DG package rejection rate for non-compliance ≤2% of DG shipments; lithium battery state-of-charge verification rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lithium battery shipments (Class 9, UN3480/3481) account for >40% of DG non-compliance findings; IATA DGR Sec 3.9 requires state-of-charge ≤30% which is physically unverifiable without specialised equipment, creating acceptance risk

l4_steps.name: Check Operator Acceptance Policy & Forbidden DG List
l4_steps.input: DG classification, operator Cargo Acceptance Policy manual, forbidden items registry
l4_steps.output: Operator acceptance or rejection decision; special approval requirement flagged if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Operator policy compliance rate 100%; forbidden item interception rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Individual airlines maintain forbidden DG lists that exceed IATA minimums; policy updates are not always propagated to the CargoWise rules engine in real time, creating a window where inadvertent acceptance of operator-prohibited DG is possible

l4_steps.name: Verify Aircraft Type DG Limits (PAX vs CAO)
l4_steps.input: DG class and quantity, aircraft registration, flight number
l4_steps.output: Aircraft-specific DG quantity limits confirmed per IATA DGR Table 2.3; PAX/CAO classification applied
l4_steps.kpi: Per-aircraft DG limit compliance rate 100%; last-minute aircraft swap DG re-check completion rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed fleet operations mean PAX aircraft quantity limits are significantly more restrictive than CAO limits for the same DG class; last-minute aircraft swaps change applicable limits and require full re-validation — Altéa DCS does not automatically trigger re-check on tail number change

l4_steps.name: Validate State & Overflight DG Restrictions for Routing
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (state restriction and NOTAMs database)
l4_steps.input: Flight routing waypoints, DG class, UN number, quantity
l4_steps.output: State variation compliance confirmation or routing conflict advisory
l4_steps.kpi: State restriction check completion rate 100% per DG-carrying flight; overflight violation rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR Addendum for State Variations is updated bi-annually but some states (notably China CAAC and several Middle East CAAs) impose interim restrictions not captured in the published addendum, requiring manual dispatcher lookup against state CAA circulars

l4_steps.name: Confirm Operator Approval for Restricted DG Classes
l4_steps.input: DG class requiring specific operator approval (Class 1 explosives, Class 7 radioactive, infectious substances)
l4_steps.output: Operator approval number confirmed and recorded; CAA authorisation obtained if required
l4_steps.kpi: Approval verification cycle time ≤4 hours for restricted classes; approval expiry miss rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Class 7 radioactive material requires Transport Index calculations and specific CAA approvals that expire; renewal tracking at most carriers relies on manual spreadsheets with no system-enforced expiry alert in CargoWise, creating regulatory exposure under IATA DGR Sec 10.8

l4_steps.name: Assign ULD Position per DG Segregation Rules
l4_steps.input: DG class, quantity, ULD type, aircraft hold configuration, passenger manifest
l4_steps.output: DG ULD or bulk position assignment in hold; preliminary centre-of-gravity impact noted
l4_steps.kpi: DG stowage compliance rate 100%; CG deviation ≤±0.5% MAC from target
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa LoadPlanner's DG segregation module requires manual overrides when multiple incompatible DG classes are present on the same flight; there is no automated incompatibility alert in the base LoadPlanner configuration, relying entirely on load controller knowledge

l4_steps.name: Run DG Compatibility Matrix Check Across All Shipments
l4_steps.input: All DG shipments on the flight, IATA DGR Table 9.3 segregation matrix
l4_steps.output: Compatibility check result; stowage conflict report if incompatible DG classes co-located
l4_steps.kpi: Segregation non-conformance rate 0%; compatibility check cycle time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR Table 9.3 covers 49 hazard class combinations; Altéa LoadPlanner automates checks for only 12 primary class pairs, requiring manual cross-reference for mixed-class loads — a high-error-risk step during high-density cargo operations

l4_steps.name: Calculate Total DG Quantities vs Aircraft Hold Limits
l4_steps.input: All assigned DG ULD positions, per-hold DG limits from aircraft type profile
l4_steps.output: DG quantity compliance summary per hold compartment; net explosive mass (NEM) calculation where applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Per-hold DG limit compliance 100%; NEM calculation accuracy within ±1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cumulative DG quantity limits per hold require aggregating across multiple individual shipments; there is no automated per-hold summation in standard Altéa LoadPlanner, exposing load controllers to arithmetic error risk on high-volume DG flights

l4_steps.name: Generate NOTOC Draft in IATA Standard Format
l4_steps.input: Confirmed DG positions, classes, UN numbers, quantities, stowage locations from load plan
l4_steps.output: Draft NOTOC (Notice to Captain) in IATA-standard format ready for dispatcher review
l4_steps.kpi: NOTOC generation time ≤15 min after load plan finalised; NOTOC accuracy rate ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTOC format requirements vary by state CAA — some authorities (FAA, EASA) require additional supplementary fields beyond the IATA standard template; Altéa NOTOC templates are not always maintained to reflect the latest state-specific variants, requiring manual addenda

l4_steps.name: Dispatcher DG Load Authorization Sign-Off
l4_steps.input: DG compliance checklist, NOTOC draft, load plan, dispatcher training currency record
l4_steps.output: Signed DG load authorization record; compliance checklist archived
l4_steps.kpi: Authorization completion ≥D-45 min (45 min before departure); 100% sign-off completion rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ICAO Annex 18 and 49 CFR Part 172 require dispatchers to hold current DG recurrent training (every 24 months); expired training certificates are not always flagged in Altéa DCS against the authorising dispatcher's profile, creating a silent regulatory non-compliance risk

l4_steps.name: Transmit NOTOC to Captain via ACARS Datalink
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS (aircraft communications and reporting system)
l4_steps.input: Finalised NOTOC, captain ACARS uplink address, departure gate
l4_steps.output: NOTOC delivered to flight deck with ACARS delivery confirmation timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: NOTOC ACARS delivery confirmation rate ≥99%; delivery completed ≥D-30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS uplink to an aircraft on the ground can fail when avionics are in pre-power state during early turnaround; backup paper NOTOC delivery via physical runner to the gate adds 15–20 min and relies on ramp coordination that frequently breaks down at congested hubs

l4_steps.name: Captain Reviews and Accepts NOTOC
l4_steps.input: NOTOC received via ACARS or EFB datalink; DG policy briefing from dispatcher
l4_steps.output: Captain acceptance acknowledgement or rejection with stated reason
l4_steps.kpi: Captain NOTOC rejection rate <1% of DG flights; acceptance completed ≥D-20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Under ICAO Annex 18 and FAR 121.285 the captain has absolute authority to offload DG; rejections after DG is physically loaded require ramp return and cause an average 35-min departure delay — root cause is often insufficient pre-departure DG briefing to the cockpit crew

l4_steps.name: Ramp Agent Loads DG per NOTOC Stowage Instructions
l4_steps.input: Finalised NOTOC, ULD build sheets, Loading Instruction Report (LIR)
l4_steps.output: DG ULDs or bulk items loaded at designated hold positions as per NOTOC
l4_steps.kpi: DG loading position accuracy 100%; loading completion ≥D-25 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp teams handle DG orientation labels and class placards under intense time pressure; IATA DGR Sec 9.3 requires 'This Way Up' orientation labels on liquid DG — compliance miss rates spike during peak turn operations when the same ramp team handles multiple aircraft simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Verify DG Load Position and Condition Post-Loading
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS — loading confirmation module)
l4_steps.input: NOTOC stowage locations, physical hold inspection, DG condition checklist
l4_steps.output: DG load verification sign-off; discrepancy or damage report if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: DG load verification completion rate 100% ≥D-20 min; discrepancy rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Hold access for DG load verification requires DG-certified personnel per IATA DGR Sec 9.4; at out-stations with thin staffing the verification is sometimes conducted by non-certified ramp agents, constituting a regulatory non-compliance that is rarely detected until a line audit

l4_steps.name: Update Final Loadsheet with Confirmed DG Positions
l4_steps.input: Verified DG hold positions, ULD manifest, passenger and cargo weights
l4_steps.output: Final signed loadsheet with DG positions confirmed; takeoff weight and CG transmitted to cockpit
l4_steps.kpi: Loadsheet finalisation ≥D-15 min; weight discrepancy vs actual ≤0 kg
l4_steps.pain_point: Late DG offloads — triggered by captain rejection or discovered package damage — require full loadsheet reissue; Altéa DCS reissue and re-signature cycle averages 8–12 min, severely compressing the pre-departure critical path and contributing to D0 departure misses

l4_steps.name: Transmit DG Manifest to Destination & En Route Stations
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS / Amadeus Altéa DCS (inter-station messaging)
l4_steps.input: Final NOTOC, DG manifest with UN numbers, classes, quantities and positions
l4_steps.output: DG advance notification transmitted to destination and en route handling agents
l4_steps.kpi: Destination DG advance notification lead time ≥2 hours before scheduled arrival (IATA RP 1654); transmission success rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA RP 1654 requires advance DG notification to the destination station; system-to-system messaging reliability degrades at stations running legacy DCS versions incompatible with modern SITA XML message formats, requiring manual telephone or email follow-up that is frequently missed

l4_steps.name: File DG Occurrence Report if Incident Detected
l4_steps.system: Safety Management System (SMS) integrated with ECCAIRS (EU) or FAA ASRS (US)
l4_steps.input: DG handling incident, package damage, leakage, or undeclared DG discovery during loading
l4_steps.output: DG occurrence report filed per ICAO Annex 18 Chapter 14 and applicable national CAA requirements
l4_steps.kpi: DG incident reporting compliance 100%; report filed ≤72 hours of incident per ICAO Annex 18
l4_steps.pain_point: DG incident under-reporting is a recognised industry-wide issue; ramp and cargo staff are reluctant to self-report fearing personal liability — airlines that have not established non-punitive SMS reporting cultures consistently show under-reporting rates estimated at 60–80% of actual DG incidents

l4_steps.name: Archive DG Documentation per Regulatory Retention Policy
l4_steps.system: CargoWise (document archive and retention management module)
l4_steps.input: NOTOC, shipper DG declarations, acceptance checklist, captain sign-off, loading verification
l4_steps.output: DG documentation set archived with jurisdiction-appropriate retention flag applied
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation archival rate 100% within 4 hours of flight departure; retrieval time for audit requests ≤2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR mandates minimum 3-month retention while FAA 49 CFR Part 175 requires 2 years and some EASA states require longer; carriers operating across jurisdictions must apply the longest applicable period globally, but CargoWise retention defaults are often configured to the shortest period, creating audit exposure
